title: Quantum phases in endofullerene zigzag chains
authors: Tobias Serwatka, Muhammad Shaeer Moeed, Roger G. Melko, Pierre-Nicholas Roy
abstract: We employ large-scale density matrix renormalization group calculations to study the quantum phases of dipolar molecules confined in bent (zigzag) endofullerene chains, as a function of the chain angle $γ$. For LiF, ferroelectric order persists across the full range $60^\circ < γ180^\circ$, with the critical effective dipole moment increasing as the chain bends and parallel alignment becomes less favorable. Near the equilateral configuration ($γ= 60^\circ$), geometric frustration drives a transition to an antiferroelectric Néel-ordered phase in which neighboring dipoles anti-align along the chain axis. We show that capturing this reorientation requires including dipolar couplings beyond the nearest-neighbor approximation, since next-nearest-neighbor interactions become equally strong at $γ= 60^\circ$. For confined water, o-D$_2$O reproduces both ordered phases, whereas p-H$_2$O -- owing to its large rotational constants -- develops no order at any chain angle despite the enhanced coordination of the bent geometry. Because a zigzag chain is the narrowest stripe of a two-dimensional lattice, these results suggest that engineered endofullerene layers could host a rich variety of dipole-ordered quantum phases beyond the ferroelectric ordering observed in previous work.
summary: The research uses advanced DMRG simulations to map the quantum phase diagram of dipolar molecules confined in curved endofullerene chains. By varying the chain angle ($\gamma$), the system undergoes transitions between ferroelectric and antiferroelectric ordered states, demonstrating that geometry dictates complex magnetic ordering in nanoscale materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the quantum phases of dipolar molecules confined within bent (zigzag) endofullerene chains as a function of the chain's geometric bending angle ($\gamma$).
main_result: The system exhibits rich dipole-ordered quantum phases, transitioning from ferroelectric to antiferroelectric order at $\gamma=60^\circ$, with specific molecular properties determining the stability of these orders.
method: Large-scale Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) calculations are employed to analyze the ground state and phase transitions across varying chain geometries.
model_or_system: The system models dipolar molecules ($	ext{LiF}$, $	ext{H}_2	ext{O}$) confined in quasi-1D zigzag chains formed by endofullerene cages. The physics is governed by dipole-dipole interactions and the geometric constraint imposed by the bending angle $\gamma$.
key_observables: Polarization (axial/scaled), Binder parameter ($U_z$), von Neumann entanglement entropy, and correlation functions.
important_parameters: Chain angle ($\gamma$) ranging from $60^\circ$ to $180^\circ$; effective dipole moment ($\mu_{	ext{eff}}$); nearest-neighbor vs. next-nearest-neighbor coupling strength.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on treating the system via a Matrix Product State (MPS) representation suitable for DMRG calculations, and assumes that dipolar interactions are the dominant physics.
figures_summary: Figures likely show polarization measurements confirming ferroelectric alignment ($\cos	heta \approx 1$) at large $\gamma$ and antiferroelectric anti-alignment ($\cos	heta \approx -1$) at $\gamma=60^\circ$, alongside Binder cumulant plots locating the quantum phase transition.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes different molecular species ($	ext{LiF}$, $	ext{o-D}_2	ext{O}$) across a range of bending angles, using DMRG to map out transitions between ferroelectric and antiferroelectric ordered states, paying special attention to the critical role of NNN interactions at $60^\circ$.
why_interesting: This work connects fundamental concepts from quantum magnetism (Néel ordering, frustration) with materials science by proposing that engineered carbon nanostructures can host tunable dipole-ordered quantum phases.
